Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

whoever pronoun

also whoever you are, anyone who, whosoever

classical

Plaut. Amph. 309b: Quisquis homō hūc profectō vēnerit, pugnōs edet.
Sen. Ep. 20.13: quisquis exit in lūcem

quisquis

relative pronoun, with a verb of its own; neuter quicquid

Quisquis es, whoever you are, is the polite way to address a stranger (Plaut. Men. 278b). “Anyone who” in a condition is often sī quis (see “someone”).

Other words

  • quīcumque, quaecumque, quodcumque — whoever, whatever person

    relative pronoun · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.31.3: quīcumque is est, eī mē profiteor inimīcum

Examples

  • Quisquis homō hūc profectō vēnerit, pugnōs edet.

    Whoever comes this way, believe me, will get a taste of my fists.Plaut. Amph. 309b

  • Dī tē amābunt quisquis es.

    Heaven bless you, whoever you are.Plaut. Men. 278b

  • Quisquis es, quidquid tibi nōmen est, senex

    Whoever you are, whatever your name is, old manPlaut. Men. 811

  • nēmō nāscitur dīves; quisquis exit in lūcem jussus est lacte et pannō esse contentus

    no one is born rich; whoever comes into the light is told to be content with milk and a ragSen. Ep. 20.13

See also whatever, who, someone.
